scope: Headless production Chromium with real AudioWorklet/native Csound, realtime_4; separate 4-CPU/2-GiB/64-MiB containers sharing Docker Desktop/host. Single began earlier; its first part predates parallel startup. No builds or test suites overlapped playback.
limitations: Concurrent containers are not physical-core isolation; parallel startup occurs during the single trace.
API preparation normalizes the master grid; both browser arms use identical authored fixture input. The lower-level native benchmark has a different event preparation path.
Headless AudioWorklet consumption is not sound-device or input-to-audible latency measurement.
Only one heavy workload has a 30-minute parallel browser run here. The conservative evidence predicate requires two clean paired workloads.
The single baseline already underruns before the explicit CPU pulse, so a matched clean-baseline stress/recovery latency comparison is unavailable.
